An oil tank is leaking $q(t)$ liters of oil after $t$ hours.
 The graph of $q(t)$ is shown above.

Approximate the rate at which the oil is leaking from the tank when $t=2$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{q}^{′}(t)≈\frac{q(t+h)-q(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 
at the time $t=2$ and step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}^{′}(2) & ≈\frac{q(2+1)-q(2-1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{q(3)-q(1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{3-2}{2} \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of leaking at the instant of time $t=2$ is $0.5\,\text{liters}/\text{hour}.$

questions.problem:
A car travels on a straight road in such a way that its position, in meters, after $t$ seconds is given by the function $f(t).$ The values of $f(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| **$t$** | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ | $12$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(t)$ | $1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $14$ | $15$ |

$$

$$

Approximate the velocity ${f}^{′}(t)$ at the point $t=4$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(t)≈\frac{f(t+h)-f(t-h)}{2h},
$$

at the time $t=4$ with step size $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(4) & ≈\frac{f(4+2)-f(4-2)}{2(2)} \\  & =\frac{f(6)-f(2)}{4} \\  & =\frac{4-1}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4} \\  & =0.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of the car at the instant of time $t=4$ is $0.75\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h},
$$

at the point $x=4$ with step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(4) & ≈\frac{f(4+1)-f(4-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{f(5)-f(3)}{2} \\  & =\frac{4-0}{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
